hazard.hazard: Unintended bolus delivered while pump is in standby.
hazard.hazardous_situation: Pump delivers an armed PCA bolus while in standby, unattended by the clinician.
hazard.hazardous_sequence_of_events: 1. Clinician arms a PCA bolus. 2. Pump transitions to standby before delivery. 3. Standby transition fails to clear the armed-bolus flag. 4. The armed bolus is delivered unattended.
hazard.software_related_causes: Standby state-transition routine does not reset the armed-bolus flag (state-machine defect).
hazard.risk_control_measures: REQ-PUMP-101: the standby transition SHALL clear any armed bolus and SHALL record the clear event.
hazard.demonstration_of_effectiveness: TC-PUMP-101-A (armed bolus cleared on standby), TC-PUMP-101-B (clear event logged), TC-PUMP-101-C (boundary: standby entered during the arming window).
hazard.residual_risk_acceptability: Acceptable per GQP-10-02; verified clearing of the armed-bolus flag on every standby transition reduces probability to Remote; residual risk is outweighed by the clinical benefit of PCA therapy.

requirements.text: The standby transition SHALL clear any armed bolus and SHALL record the clear event in the audit log.

test_cases.description: Armed bolus is cleared when the pump enters standby.
test_cases.setup: Arm a 2 mL bolus; place pump in standby.
test_cases.expectedResults: Armed-bolus flag is cleared; no delivery occurs.

test_cases.description: Clear event is written to the audit log.
test_cases.expectedResults: Audit log contains a bolus-clear record with timestamp.

test_cases.description: Boundary: standby entered exactly during the arming window.
test_cases.setup: Enter standby at the arming/deliver boundary.
test_cases.steps: 1. Arm. 2. Enter standby within the same control cycle.
test_cases.expectedResults: Armed-bolus flag is cleared; no bolus is delivered.

design_docs.name: bolus delivery control - Software Design Description
design_docs.description:
The bolus delivery control module governs the arming and delivery of a patient- or clinician-requested bolus and its interaction with the pump's operating modes. Its scope is limited to managing the armed-bolus state and gating delivery on the current operating mode; it does not compute dose magnitude or drive the pump mechanism directly. Under IEC 62304 it is a controlled software component whose behavior must be specified and verified, and in ISO 14971 terms it mitigates the hazard of an unintended or unattended bolus delivery that can lead to overdose.

At runtime the module moves through an idle state, an armed state entered when a bolus is requested, a delivering state, and an inhibited state entered on transitions to standby, alarm, or fault conditions. Mode transitions are events that must deterministically clear or hold the armed-bolus flag: any transition away from an active-delivery mode fails safe by clearing the armed request and recording the clear, so that no residual armed state can later resolve into an unattended delivery. The module recommits to delivery only from an explicit, attended arm event.

The component decomposition comprises an arm/disarm state manager, a mode-transition observer, an audit-logging hook, and a delivery-gate interface to the actuation layer. Verification hooks for the test suite include injectable mode-transition events, an observable armed-bolus flag, and a readable audit trail, so that the suite can assert the flag is cleared on every standby/alarm/fault transition, that the clear is logged, and that a delivery is issued only from an attended arm.

user_needs.text: As a clinician, I need the pump to never deliver a bolus unless I have intentionally armed and attended it, so that a patient is not harmed by an unattended dose.

system_requirements.text: The infusion system SHALL prevent delivery of an armed bolus once the device leaves an attended active-delivery mode.
The infusion system SHALL create an audit record whenever an armed bolus is cleared by a mode transition.

hazard.hazard: Downstream occlusion not detected; analgesia silently interrupted.
hazard.hazardous_situation: Occlusion goes undetected and PCA analgesia is silently interrupted.
hazard.hazardous_sequence_of_events: 1. Downstream line occludes. 2. Line pressure rises above 15 psi. 3. The occlusion detector must alarm within 2 seconds. 4. If undetected, prescribed analgesia is not delivered.
hazard.software_related_causes: Pressure-sampling task could miss the 2-second alarm deadline under peak CPU load.
hazard.risk_control_measures: REQ-PUMP-102: an occlusion SHALL be detected and alarmed within 2 seconds of line pressure exceeding 15 psi.
hazard.demonstration_of_effectiveness: TC-PUMP-102-A (alarm within 2 s), TC-PUMP-102-B (boundary: 15.0 vs 15.1 psi), TC-PUMP-102-C (negative: sensor disconnect raises a fault).
hazard.residual_risk_acceptability: Acceptable; 2-second bounded detection verified under worst-case scheduling load reduces probability to Remote.

requirements.text: An occlusion SHALL be detected and alarmed within 2 seconds of line pressure exceeding 15 psi.

test_cases.expectedResults: Alarm annunciates within 2 seconds.
No alarm at 15.0 psi; alarm at 15.1 psi.
Pump raises a sensor-fault alarm and does not mask occlusion detection.

design_docs.name: occlusion detection - Software Design Description
design_docs.description:
The occlusion detection module monitors downstream line pressure and raises an alarm when a blockage is present, so that an interrupted infusion is surfaced to the clinician. Its scope is the acquisition and evaluation of pressure samples and the timely annunciation of an occlusion; it does not itself clear the blockage. As an IEC 62304 controlled component it must meet a specified detection latency, and under ISO 14971 it mitigates the hazard of an undetected therapy interruption leading to under-treatment.

The module operates as a periodic sampling task that transitions between a monitoring state, an occlusion-suspected state when pressure crosses a configured limit, an alarming state once the condition persists, and a fault state when the sensor is implausible or unavailable. Detection is bounded by a configured deadline, and the design fails safe by treating sensor loss or scheduling starvation as a fault that alarms rather than as a silent normal reading.

The decomposition comprises a pressure-sampling driver, a threshold evaluator, a debounce/persistence filter, an alarm annunciator, and a sensor-health monitor. Verification hooks include injectable pressure traces and sensor-fault stimuli, an observable alarm state, and a measurable detection latency, letting the test suite assert alarm timing under worst-case load, correct behavior around the configured limit, and a fault alarm on sensor disconnect.

user_needs.text: As a clinician, I need to be promptly alerted when the line is blocked, so that a silent interruption of analgesia does not leave the patient in untreated pain.

system_requirements.text: The infusion system SHALL detect and annunciate a downstream occlusion within a specified time of the pressure exceeding its configured limit.
The infusion system SHALL annunciate a fault when the pressure sensor is unavailable or implausible rather than suppressing occlusion detection.

hazard.hazard: Dose computed from an out-of-range drug concentration.
hazard.hazardous_situation: Pump computes and delivers a dose from an out-of-range drug concentration.
hazard.function: Drug concentration entry and dose calculation
hazard.hazardous_sequence_of_events: 1. Clinician enters the drug concentration. 2. A value outside the approved 0.1-10 mg/mL range is entered. 3. Dose calculation uses the out-of-range value. 4. The pump delivers an incorrect dose.
hazard.software_related_causes: Missing range validation on the commanded concentration input allows an out-of-range value into the dose calculation.
hazard.risk_control_measures: REQ-PUMP-103: the pump SHALL reject drug concentrations outside 0.1-10 mg/mL and SHALL require re-entry.
hazard.demonstration_of_effectiveness: TC-PUMP-103-A (valid value accepted), TC-PUMP-103-B (boundary: 0.1 and 10.0 accepted; 0.09 and 10.1 rejected), TC-PUMP-103-C (negative: non-numeric input rejected).
hazard.residual_risk_acceptability: Acceptable; enforced range validation blocks out-of-range concentrations, reducing probability to Remote.

requirements.text: The pump SHALL reject drug concentrations outside the range 0.1-10 mg/mL and SHALL require re-entry before dosing.

test_cases.expectedResults: Value accepted; dosing proceeds.
0.1 and 10.0 accepted; 0.09 and 10.1 rejected with re-entry prompt.
Input rejected; re-entry required.

design_docs.name: drug concentration entry and dose calculation - Software Design Description
design_docs.description:
The drug concentration entry and dose calculation module validates clinician-entered concentration values and derives the delivery parameters used by downstream dosing logic. Its scope is limited to input validation, unit handling, and deterministic calculation; it does not initiate therapy. As an IEC 62304 controlled component it must reject unsafe inputs before they influence a dose, and under ISO 14971 it mitigates the hazard of over- or under-dose arising from an out-of-range or malformed concentration.

At runtime the module transitions through an awaiting-input state, a validating state, a calculation-ready state once a coherent input set is present, and a rejected state when a value falls outside its configured acceptable range or fails a plausibility check. It recalculates only from a validated input set and otherwise fails closed by withholding a computed result and prompting re-entry, so an invalid concentration can never reach the dosing path.

The decomposition comprises an input normalizer, a range and plausibility validator, a calculation engine, and an output publisher that emits the result with status metadata. Verification hooks include injectable concentration values, controllable range configuration, and an observable accept/reject outcome, enabling the test suite to assert acceptance of valid values, rejection at the configured boundaries, and rejection of non-numeric or incoherent input.

user_needs.text: As a clinician, I need the pump to refuse an out-of-range drug concentration, so that a data-entry error cannot produce an unsafe dose.

system_requirements.text: The infusion system SHALL reject a drug concentration outside its configured acceptable range and SHALL require re-entry before dosing.

hazard.hazard: Cumulative in-line air exceeds the safe limit without a pump halt.
hazard.hazardous_situation: Cumulative infused air exceeds the 100 microliter safe limit without a pump halt.
hazard.hazardous_sequence_of_events: 1. Air enters the infusion line. 2. The air-volume accumulator tracks cumulative air. 3. The pump must halt when cumulative air exceeds 100 microliters. 4. If the accumulator wraps and under-counts, air is infused.
hazard.software_related_causes: The air-volume accumulator could overflow and wrap, under-counting cumulative air.
hazard.risk_control_measures: REQ-PUMP-104: the pump SHALL halt infusion and alarm when cumulative in-line air exceeds 100 microliters; the accumulator SHALL saturate rather than wrap.
hazard.demonstration_of_effectiveness: TC-PUMP-104-A (halt above 100 uL), TC-PUMP-104-B (boundary: 100 vs 101 uL), TC-PUMP-104-C (negative: accumulator saturates at max, no wrap).
hazard.residual_risk_acceptability: Acceptable; saturating accumulator and bounded halt verified, reducing probability to Improbable.

requirements.text: The pump SHALL halt infusion and alarm when cumulative in-line air exceeds 100 microliters, and the air-volume accumulator SHALL saturate at its maximum rather than wrap.

test_cases.expectedResults: Pump halts and alarms.
No halt at 100 uL; halt at 101 uL.
Accumulator saturates at max; no wrap; pump remains halted.

design_docs.name: air-in-line detection - Software Design Description
design_docs.description:
The air-in-line detection module tracks the volume of air passing the fluid-path sensor and halts infusion when accumulated air reaches a configured safe limit. Its scope is the accumulation and evaluation of detected air and the commanded halt; it does not remove air from the line. As an IEC 62304 controlled component its accumulator arithmetic must be robust, and under ISO 14971 it mitigates the hazard of venous air embolism from infused air.

The module runs as a sampling task with a monitoring state, an accumulating state, a halting state once the configured limit is exceeded, and a fault state on sensor loss. A central design property is that the cumulative-air accumulator saturates at its maximum representable value rather than wrapping, so that a large or sustained air event cannot roll the count back under the limit; the module fails safe by halting and alarming on both an over-limit condition and a sensor fault.

The decomposition comprises an air-sensor driver, a saturating cumulative accumulator, a limit comparator, a halt-command interface, and a sensor-health monitor. Verification hooks include injectable air-volume profiles and sensor faults, an observable accumulator value, and an observable halt state, so the test suite can assert the halt above the configured limit, correct behavior at the boundary, and accumulator saturation without wrap under an overflow stimulus.

user_needs.text: As a patient, I need the pump to stop before a harmful amount of air reaches me, so that I am not exposed to an air embolism.

system_requirements.text: The infusion system SHALL halt infusion and alarm when cumulative in-line air exceeds its configured safe limit.
The infusion system SHALL ensure the cumulative-air measurement saturates rather than wraps under a sustained air event.

hazard.hazard: Uncontrolled gravity free-flow when the cassette is removed.
hazard.hazardous_situation: Uncontrolled gravity free-flow of drug occurs when the cassette is removed.
hazard.hazardous_sequence_of_events: 1. Clinician opens the pump door. 2. The anti-free-flow valve must engage before the latch releases. 3. Software must confirm the valve closed before releasing the door latch. 4. If the latch releases first, gravity free-flow delivers uncontrolled drug.
hazard.software_related_causes: Door-latch release could be commanded before the valve-closed confirmation is read.
hazard.risk_control_measures: REQ-PUMP-105: the door latch SHALL NOT release until the anti-free-flow valve reports closed.
hazard.demonstration_of_effectiveness: TC-PUMP-105-A (latch blocked until valve closed), TC-PUMP-105-B (boundary: valve-close confirmation timeout), TC-PUMP-105-C (negative: valve fault holds the latch closed).
hazard.residual_risk_acceptability: Acceptable; interlock verified so the latch cannot release before valve confirmation, reducing probability to Remote.

requirements.text: The door latch SHALL NOT release until the anti-free-flow valve reports a closed state.

test_cases.setup: Request door open with valve open.
test_cases.expectedResults: Latch remains engaged until valve reports closed.

test_cases.setup: Delay the valve-closed signal to the timeout limit.
test_cases.expectedResults: Latch remains closed and a fault is raised at timeout.
Latch remains closed; fault alarm raised.

design_docs.name: free-flow protection interlock - Software Design Description
design_docs.description:
The free-flow protection interlock module coordinates the mechanical anti-free-flow valve with the door latch so that the fluid path cannot be opened to uncontrolled gravity flow. Its scope is the sequencing and confirmation of valve and latch state; it does not itself seal the fluid path. As an IEC 62304 controlled component it must enforce a strict ordering, and under ISO 14971 it mitigates the hazard of an uncontrolled free-flow overdose when the set is removed.

At runtime the module holds a closed-and-latched state, a release-requested state, and a released state that is only reachable after the valve reports closed; a timeout or valve fault drives an inhibited state that keeps the latch engaged. The interlock fails safe by never releasing the latch on an unconfirmed or timed-out valve signal, so a missing confirmation holds the path closed rather than opening it.

The decomposition comprises a valve-state reader, a latch-command interface, a sequencing controller, and a timeout/fault handler. Verification hooks include injectable valve-position signals and fault stimuli, an observable latch state, and controllable timeouts, allowing the test suite to assert that the latch stays engaged until the valve confirms closed, that a confirmation timeout raises a fault and holds the latch, and that a valve fault keeps the path closed.

user_needs.text: As a clinician, I need the set to be safe against free-flow whenever I open the pump, so that removing the cassette cannot deliver an uncontrolled dose.

system_requirements.text: The infusion system SHALL prevent release of the door latch until the anti-free-flow valve is confirmed closed.

hazard.hazard: Pump stops on battery depletion without a prior alarm.
hazard.hazardous_situation: Pump stops on battery depletion without raising a prior low-battery alarm.
hazard.hazardous_sequence_of_events: 1. Mains power is lost. 2. The battery discharges. 3. At 10% state-of-charge the pump must alarm and continue for at least 30 minutes. 4. If it stops silently, therapy is interrupted unnoticed.
hazard.software_related_causes: The battery gauge could report a stale state-of-charge if its sampling task starves.
hazard.risk_control_measures: REQ-PUMP-106: at 10% state-of-charge the pump SHALL raise a low-battery alarm and SHALL sustain infusion for at least 30 minutes.
hazard.demonstration_of_effectiveness: TC-PUMP-106-A (alarm at 10%), TC-PUMP-106-B (boundary: 10 vs 9%), TC-PUMP-106-C (negative: gauge fault triggers a conservative alarm).
hazard.residual_risk_acceptability: Acceptable; bounded alarm and 30-minute sustain verified, reducing probability of silent interruption to Remote.

requirements.text: At 10% battery state-of-charge the pump SHALL raise a low-battery alarm and SHALL sustain infusion for at least 30 minutes.

test_cases.expectedResults: Low-battery alarm annunciates.
Alarm at 10%; infusion continues; escalation below 10%.
Pump raises a conservative low-battery alarm rather than trusting the stale value.

design_docs.name: low-battery power management - Software Design Description
design_docs.description:
The low-battery power management module monitors the battery state of charge and ensures the clinician is warned, with a guaranteed reserve of continued operation, before power is exhausted. Its scope is charge estimation, alarm annunciation, and reserve management; it does not control charging hardware. As an IEC 62304 controlled component it must not silently stop, and under ISO 14971 it mitigates the hazard of an unnoticed therapy interruption from power loss.

The module transitions between a normal-power state, a low-battery state entered at a configured charge threshold, an on-reserve state that sustains infusion for a specified minimum time while alarming, and a gauge-fault state. It fails safe by treating a stale or implausible charge estimate as a conservative low-battery condition, so uncertainty raises an alarm early rather than trusting an optimistic reading.

The decomposition comprises a fuel-gauge sampler, a threshold and hysteresis evaluator, an alarm annunciator, and a reserve-time monitor. Verification hooks include an injectable charge signal and gauge faults, an observable alarm state, and a measurable sustain time, so the test suite can assert the alarm at the configured threshold, continued infusion across the reserve, and a conservative alarm on a gauge fault.

user_needs.text: As a clinician, I need a clear warning and a period of continued operation before the battery dies, so that therapy is never silently interrupted by power loss.

system_requirements.text: The infusion system SHALL raise a low-battery alarm at a configured charge threshold and SHALL sustain infusion for a specified minimum time thereafter.
The infusion system SHALL treat an implausible battery-charge estimate as a conservative low-battery condition.

hazard.hazard: Demand bolus delivered within the programmed lockout interval.
hazard.hazardous_situation: A demand bolus is delivered within the programmed lockout interval, stacking doses.
hazard.hazardous_sequence_of_events: 1. Patient presses the demand button and a bolus is delivered. 2. Within the lockout interval the patient presses again. 3. The lockout must ignore the second request. 4. If the lockout is bypassed, a second bolus stacks.
hazard.software_related_causes: The lockout timer could be reset by a spurious button-debounce event, re-enabling an early demand.
hazard.risk_control_measures: REQ-PUMP-107: demand boluses within the programmed lockout interval SHALL be ignored and logged; debounce SHALL NOT reset the lockout timer.
hazard.demonstration_of_effectiveness: TC-PUMP-107-A (early demand ignored), TC-PUMP-107-B (boundary: request at exactly lockout expiry accepted; 1 s before rejected), TC-PUMP-107-C (negative: rapid double-press does not reset the timer).
hazard.residual_risk_acceptability: Acceptable; lockout enforcement verified against debounce interference, reducing probability of dose stacking to Remote.

requirements.text: Demand boluses requested within the programmed lockout interval SHALL be ignored and logged, and button debounce SHALL NOT reset the lockout timer.

test_cases.setup: Deliver a bolus; press again within lockout.
test_cases.expectedResults: Second request ignored and logged.

test_cases.setup: Press 1 s before and at expiry.
test_cases.steps: 1. Press at T-1s. 2. Press at T.
test_cases.expectedResults: Rejected before expiry; accepted at expiry.
Lockout timer is not reset; no early bolus.

design_docs.name: PCA demand and lockout enforcement - Software Design Description
design_docs.description:
The PCA demand and lockout enforcement module processes patient demand requests and enforces the lockout interval that prevents dose stacking. Its scope is the handling of demand events and the timing of the lockout; it does not compute bolus magnitude. As an IEC 62304 controlled component the lockout timing must be tamper-resistant, and under ISO 14971 it mitigates the hazard of opioid overdose from repeated demands within the lockout window.

The module holds an available state in which a demand yields a bolus, and a locked-out state entered after a delivery that ignores and logs further demands until the configured interval elapses. A key design property is that input debounce and spurious button events must not reset or shorten the lockout timer; the module fails safe by rejecting a demand whenever the interval has not verifiably elapsed.

The decomposition comprises a demand-button handler with debounce, a monotonic lockout timer, a demand-arbitration gate, and an event logger. Verification hooks include injectable demand and chatter events, an observable lockout state, and a readable event log, enabling the test suite to assert that early demands are ignored and logged, that a demand at the interval boundary is honored, and that button chatter never resets the timer.

user_needs.text: As a patient using PCA, I need the pump to enforce the lockout between doses, so that repeated button presses cannot stack into an overdose.

system_requirements.text: The infusion system SHALL ignore and log patient demands that occur within the configured lockout interval.
The infusion system SHALL ensure input debounce cannot reset or shorten the lockout interval.

hazard.hazard: Programmed rate retained instead of KVO after infusion completion.
hazard.hazardous_situation: Pump continues at the programmed rate after infusion completion instead of the keep-vein-open rate.
hazard.hazardous_sequence_of_events: 1. The programmed infusion completes. 2. The pump transitions to the KVO rate. 3. The KVO setpoint (<=5 mL/hr) must be loaded. 4. If the prior programmed rate is retained, over-infusion continues.
hazard.software_related_causes: The KVO transition could retain the prior programmed rate instead of loading the KVO setpoint.
hazard.risk_control_measures: REQ-PUMP-108: on infusion completion the pump SHALL load the KVO setpoint (<=5 mL/hr) and SHALL NOT retain the programmed rate.
hazard.demonstration_of_effectiveness: TC-PUMP-108-A (KVO setpoint loaded on completion), TC-PUMP-108-B (boundary: 5.0 vs 5.1 mL/hr), TC-PUMP-108-C (negative: setpoint-load failure alarms and stops).
hazard.residual_risk_acceptability: Acceptable; verified KVO setpoint load on completion reduces over-infusion probability to Remote. NOTE: a distinct newly-observed situation - KVO transition while an alarm-silence is active - was raised in design review but has not yet been captured as its own SHA row.

requirements.text: On infusion completion the pump SHALL load the keep-vein-open setpoint (at most 5 mL/hr) and SHALL NOT retain the programmed rate.

test_cases.expectedResults: Rate drops to the KVO setpoint (<=5 mL/hr).
5.0 accepted; 5.1 rejected as above the KVO ceiling.

test_cases.setup: Inject a setpoint-load fault at completion.
test_cases.expectedResults: Pump alarms and stops rather than continuing at the programmed rate.

design_docs.name: keep-vein-open (KVO) transition control - Software Design Description
design_docs.description:
The keep-vein-open transition control module manages the change from a programmed infusion to a low maintenance rate once delivery completes. Its scope is the detection of completion and the loading of the maintenance setpoint; it does not itself compute the therapy. As an IEC 62304 controlled component the transition must be deterministic, and under ISO 14971 it mitigates the hazard of continued over-infusion when a completed therapy fails to drop to its maintenance rate.

At runtime the module holds an infusing state, a completion-detected state, and a maintenance state in which the configured keep-vein-open setpoint is in effect; a setpoint-load fault drives an alarm-and-stop state. The design fails safe by never retaining the prior programmed rate into the maintenance phase: if the maintenance setpoint cannot be loaded, the module stops and alarms rather than continuing at the higher rate.

The decomposition comprises a completion detector, a setpoint loader, a rate-arbitration interface, and a fault handler. Verification hooks include an injectable completion event and setpoint-load faults, an observable effective rate, and an observable alarm state, so the test suite can assert that the maintenance setpoint is loaded on completion, that the ceiling is enforced, and that a load failure alarms and stops rather than retaining the programmed rate.

user_needs.text: As a clinician, I need the pump to drop to a safe maintenance rate when the infusion finishes, so that a completed therapy does not keep over-infusing.

system_requirements.text: The infusion system SHALL load the configured keep-vein-open setpoint on infusion completion and SHALL NOT retain the programmed rate.

hazard.hazard: Drug leaks from a cracked cassette housing, under-delivering the dose.
hazard.hazardous_situation: Drug leaks from a cracked cassette housing, and the prescribed dose is not fully delivered.
hazard.hazardous_sequence_of_events: 1. The cassette housing develops a hairline crack under mechanical stress. 2. Drug leaks from the fluid path. 3. The prescribed dose is not fully delivered to the patient.
hazard.software_related_causes: None - purely mechanical cause; no software contribution.
hazard.exploitability_pre_mitigation: N/A - no software or cyber cause
hazard.risk_control_measures: REQ-PUMP-109: the cassette housing SHALL withstand three times maximum operating pressure without leakage per mechanical qualification, and incoming inspection SHALL verify housing integrity.
hazard.demonstration_of_effectiveness: MECH-TC-109-A (pressure burst test), MECH-TC-109-B (drop test), incoming-inspection AQL sampling.
hazard.exploitability_post_mitigation: N/A - no software or cyber cause
hazard.residual_risk_acceptability: Acceptable; mechanical qualification and incoming inspection reduce leakage probability to Improbable. Software verification is not the closure mechanism because the cause is mechanical.

requirements.text: The cassette housing SHALL withstand three times maximum operating pressure without leakage, verified by mechanical qualification and incoming inspection.

test_cases.expectedResults: No leakage or rupture.
No cracks; no leakage under subsequent pressure test.

design_docs.name: cassette fluid-path containment - Design Description
design_docs.description:
The cassette fluid-path containment describes the mechanical design that keeps the drug fluid path sealed within the disposable cassette. Its scope is the structural integrity of the housing and its resistance to leakage under operating and handling stresses; there is no software element in this control. Under ISO 14971 it mitigates the hazard of under-delivery caused by a fluid-path leak, and it is qualified as a mechanical risk control rather than a verified software behavior.

The relevant behavior is physical rather than a runtime state model: the housing must retain containment across its rated operating pressure with a defined safety margin, and across the mechanical shocks and handling loads expected in service. The design fails safe toward containment by specifying wall structure and material properties that tolerate stress concentrations without crack initiation, and by screening incoming parts for integrity before use.

The decomposition comprises the housing structure, the sealing interfaces, and the incoming-inspection acceptance controls. Verification is by mechanical qualification rather than a test suite: pressure-integrity testing to a configured multiple of operating pressure, drop and handling testing, and sampling inspection, so that containment is demonstrated by physical evidence. Because the cause is mechanical, no software hazard path exists to verify for this control.

user_needs.text: As a patient, I need the drug container to stay sealed, so that a leak does not silently reduce my prescribed dose.

system_requirements.text: The infusion system SHALL maintain fluid-path containment across its rated operating pressure and expected handling loads, demonstrated by mechanical qualification.

hazard.hazard: Luer connector separates and analgesia is not delivered.
hazard.hazardous_situation: The luer connector separates under vibration and analgesia is not delivered to the patient.
hazard.hazardous_sequence_of_events: 1. Transport vibration loosens the luer connector. 2. The connection separates. 3. Drug is not delivered to the patient.
hazard.software_related_causes: None - mechanical connector loosening; no software contribution.
hazard.exploitability_pre_mitigation: N/A - no software or cyber cause
hazard.risk_control_measures: REQ-PUMP-110: the luer connection SHALL be a locking type qualified to retain integrity under IEC 60068 vibration, and labeling SHALL instruct connection verification.
hazard.demonstration_of_effectiveness: MECH-TC-110-A (IEC 60068 vibration retention), MECH-TC-110-B (locking-luer pull-off force), labeling verification.
hazard.exploitability_post_mitigation: N/A - no software or cyber cause
hazard.residual_risk_acceptability: Acceptable; locking luer qualified under vibration and reinforced by labeling reduces separation probability to Improbable. Software verification is not the closure mechanism because the cause is mechanical.

requirements.text: The luer connection SHALL be a locking type that retains fluid-path integrity under IEC 60068 vibration, and labeling SHALL instruct the user to verify the connection.

test_cases.setup: Subject the connection to IEC 60068 vibration profile.
test_cases.expectedResults: Connection remains intact; no separation.
Locking luer retains engagement below the failure threshold.

design_docs.name: fluid-path connection integrity - Design Description
design_docs.description:
The fluid-path connection integrity describes the mechanical design that keeps the delivery connection engaged from the pump to the patient. Its scope is the retention of the connection under vibration and handling; there is no software element in this control. Under ISO 14971 it mitigates the hazard of under-delivery caused by an inadvertent disconnection, and it is qualified as a mechanical and labeling risk control rather than a verified software behavior.

The relevant behavior is physical: a locking connection must resist loosening under the vibration and incidental loads expected in transport and use, and must require a deliberate action to disengage. The design fails safe toward retention by selecting a positive-locking connector and reinforcing correct use through labeling and a connection-verification instruction.

The decomposition comprises the locking connector, the mating interface, and the labeling/instruction control. Verification is by mechanical qualification rather than a test suite: vibration testing to a recognized profile, pull-off force characterization, and labeling verification, so that retention is demonstrated by physical evidence. Because the cause is mechanical, no software hazard path exists to verify for this control.

user_needs.text: As a patient, I need the delivery connection to stay attached during normal movement and transport, so that a disconnection does not interrupt my therapy.

system_requirements.text: The infusion system SHALL retain fluid-path connection integrity under expected vibration and handling, demonstrated by mechanical qualification and reinforced by labeling.

hazard.hazard: Alarm not annunciated.
hazard.hazardous_situation: The alarm is not annunciated.
hazard.hazardous_sequence_of_events: Alarm condition occurs.
hazard.software_related_causes: Audio driver defect.
hazard.harm: Delayed clinician response to a hazard.
hazard.risk_control_measures: REQ-PUMP-111: audible alarms SHALL reach 65 dBA at 1 metre.
hazard.demonstration_of_effectiveness: TC-PUMP-111-A (alarm loudness at 1 m).
hazard.residual_risk_acceptability: Acceptable; alarm loudness verified at 65 dBA reduces the probability of a missed alarm to Remote.

requirements.text: Audible alarms SHALL reach at least 65 dBA measured at 1 metre.

test_cases.setup: Trigger an alarm; measure SPL at 1 m.
test_cases.expectedResults: SPL is at least 65 dBA at 1 metre.

design_docs.name: audible alarm annunciation - Software Design Description
design_docs.description:
The audible alarm annunciation module produces the audible signals that draw clinician attention to an active alarm condition. Its scope is the generation and sounding of alarm tones at a specified loudness; it does not decide which conditions are alarms. As an IEC 62304 controlled component it must reliably sound an annunciation, and under ISO 14971 it mitigates the hazard of a delayed clinician response to a hazardous condition.

The module transitions between a silent state, an annunciating state driven by an active alarm, and a driver-fault state when the audio path is unavailable. It fails safe by escalating or surfacing a fault when the intended sound cannot be produced, so a defective audio path is itself made visible rather than leaving an alarm silently unheard.

The decomposition comprises an alarm-event interface, a tone generator, an audio-driver abstraction, and a driver-health monitor. Verification hooks include injectable alarm events and driver faults, an observable annunciation state, and a measurable output level, so the test suite can assert that an active alarm sounds at the specified loudness and that an audio-path fault is surfaced rather than silently swallowed.

user_needs.text: As a clinician, I need alarms to be clearly audible, so that I respond promptly to a hazardous condition.

system_requirements.text: The infusion system SHALL annunciate active alarms audibly at a specified minimum loudness.

hazard.hazard: Infusion status display freezes.
hazard.hazardous_situation: The infusion status display shows stale values.
hazard.hazardous_sequence_of_events: 1. The UI rendering thread stalls. 2. The status display stops updating. 3. Displayed values become stale.
hazard.software_related_causes: UI thread priority inversion stalls rendering.
hazard.risk_control_measures: REQ-PUMP-112: the infusion status display SHALL refresh at least once per second.
hazard.demonstration_of_effectiveness: TC-PUMP-112-A (display refresh rate), TC-PUMP-112-B (negative: rendering-thread watchdog recovers the UI).
hazard.residual_risk_acceptability: Acceptable; a rendering watchdog recovers a stalled UI and bounds staleness, reducing probability to Remote.

requirements.text: The infusion status display SHALL refresh at least once per second, and a watchdog SHALL recover a stalled rendering thread.

test_cases.expectedResults: Display refreshes at least once per second.
Watchdog fires and the UI recovers within bound.

design_docs.name: infusion status display rendering - Software Design Description
design_docs.description:
The infusion status display rendering module presents current infusion status to the clinician and keeps that presentation current. Its scope is the refresh and rendering of status values; it does not compute the underlying therapy. As an IEC 62304 controlled component it must bound the staleness of what it shows, and under ISO 14971 it mitigates the hazard of a clinician acting on outdated displayed information.

The module runs as a periodic rendering task with an updating state, a stalled state detected by a watchdog when rendering does not progress, and a recovered state after the watchdog intervenes. It fails safe by bounding how long a stale frame can persist and by recovering or flagging a stalled renderer rather than leaving frozen values on screen indefinitely.

The decomposition comprises a status data source interface, a render loop, a rendering watchdog, and a recovery handler. Verification hooks include a controllable render scheduler and injectable stalls, an observable refresh cadence, and an observable watchdog action, so the test suite can assert the nominal refresh rate and that a stalled rendering thread is detected and recovered within bound.

user_needs.text: As a clinician, I need the status display to stay current, so that I do not make a decision based on stale information.

system_requirements.text: The infusion system SHALL bound the staleness of the displayed infusion status and SHALL recover a stalled display within a specified time.

hazard.hazard: Incorrect infusion rate commanded.
hazard.hazardous_situation: Pump runs at an incorrect commanded rate.
hazard.hazardous_sequence_of_events: 1. The rate setpoint is computed. 2. A software fault corrupts the commanded rate. 3. The pump runs at the wrong rate. 4. Over- or under-infusion results.
hazard.software_related_causes: Software error.
hazard.risk_control_measures: REQ-PUMP-113: the commanded rate SHALL be range-checked and cross-verified by an independent monitor.
hazard.demonstration_of_effectiveness: TC-PUMP-113-A (range check), TC-PUMP-113-B (boundary: max rate), TC-PUMP-113-C (negative: monitor mismatch stops the pump).
hazard.residual_risk_acceptability: Acceptable; independent rate monitor and range check reduce the probability of an undetected wrong rate to Remote.

requirements.text: The commanded infusion rate SHALL be range-checked and cross-verified by an independent monitor before delivery.

test_cases.expectedResults: Rate rejected.
200 accepted; 201 rejected.
Pump stops on cross-check mismatch.

design_docs.name: dose rate command and cross-verification - Software Design Description
design_docs.description:
The dose rate command and cross-verification module produces the commanded infusion rate and validates it against an independent monitor before delivery. Its scope is the derivation, range-checking, and cross-verification of the rate; it does not drive the motor directly. As an IEC 62304 controlled component its numeric handling and monitor comparison must be specified precisely, and under ISO 14971 it mitigates the hazard of over- or under-infusion from a corrupted or miscomputed rate.

At runtime the module holds a computing state, a verifying state in which the primary command is compared with the independent monitor, a committed state on agreement, and a stopped state on disagreement or range violation. The design accounts for fixed-point scaling and rounding behavior explicitly and fails safe by stopping the pump on any cross-check mismatch rather than delivering an unverified rate.

The decomposition comprises a rate scaler with defined rounding, a range checker, an independent monitor comparator, and a stop interface. Verification hooks include injectable setpoints and induced primary/monitor divergence, an observable commit/stop outcome, and observable rounding at scale boundaries, so the test suite can assert range rejection, boundary rounding, and a stop on monitor mismatch.

user_needs.text: As a patient, I need the delivered rate to match what was prescribed, so that a software fault does not over- or under-infuse me.

system_requirements.text: The infusion system SHALL range-check the commanded rate and cross-verify it against an independent monitor before delivery.
The infusion system SHALL stop delivery when the commanded rate and its independent monitor disagree.

hazard.hazard: Unauthorized modification of dose limits.
hazard.hazardous_situation: Pump operates with an unsafe, unauthorized dose limit.
hazard.hazardous_sequence_of_events: 1. The pump receives a dose-limit configuration over the hospital network. 2. A malformed, unauthenticated message alters the hard limit. 3. The pump accepts an unsafe dose limit. 4. Overdose occurs on subsequent programming.
hazard.software_related_causes: Parsing bug in the configuration message handler.
hazard.risk_control_measures: REQ-PUMP-114: configuration messages SHALL be schema-validated before any limit is applied.
hazard.demonstration_of_effectiveness: TC-PUMP-114-A (malformed message rejected), TC-PUMP-114-B (boundary: out-of-range limit rejected).
hazard.residual_risk_acceptability: Acceptable; schema validation of configuration messages reduces the probability of an accepted malformed limit to Remote.

requirements.text: Configuration messages SHALL be schema-validated before any dose limit is applied.

test_cases.expectedResults: Message rejected; limit unchanged.

test_cases.setup: Send a limit above the hard ceiling.
test_cases.expectedResults: Limit rejected.

design_docs.name: remote dose-limit configuration handling - Software Design Description
design_docs.description:
The remote dose-limit configuration handling module receives dose-limit configuration over a network interface and applies it to the pump's safety limits. Its scope is the reception, authentication, and validation of configuration messages; it does not itself dose. As an IEC 62304 controlled component that is network-exposed, both its parsing and its message-authenticity handling are safety- and security-relevant, and under ISO 14971 it mitigates the hazard of an unsafe or unauthorized dose limit being accepted.

At runtime the module holds a listening state, an authenticating state that establishes message origin and integrity, a validating state that schema- and range-checks the payload, and an applied state; any failure drives a rejected state that leaves the current limits unchanged. The design fails safe by rejecting a message that is malformed, out of range, or of unverified origin, so an unauthenticated or invalid update cannot alter a safety limit.

The decomposition comprises a transport listener, a message-authenticity verifier, a schema and range validator, and a limit-application interface. Verification hooks include injectable malformed, out-of-range, and unauthenticated messages, an observable accept/reject outcome, and observable effective limits, so the test suite can assert rejection of malformed and out-of-range limits and that unverified-origin messages never change a limit.

user_needs.text: As a clinician, I need remotely configured dose limits to be authentic and valid, so that no one can push an unsafe limit to the pump.

system_requirements.text: The infusion system SHALL validate the structure and range of a configuration message before applying any dose limit.
The infusion system SHALL verify the authenticity and integrity of a configuration message before applying any dose limit.

hazard.hazard: Occlusion undetected due to a threshold comparison error.
hazard.hazardous_situation: An occlusion goes undetected because the pressure threshold comparison is wrong.
hazard.hazardous_sequence_of_events: 1. Downstream pressure rises. 2. An off-by-one in the threshold comparison suppresses the alarm at the limit. 3. The occlusion is not detected. 4. Analgesia is interrupted.
hazard.software_related_causes: Pressure-threshold comparison off-by-one at the 15 psi limit.
hazard.risk_control_measures: REQ-PUMP-115: the occlusion threshold comparison SHALL use an inclusive limit and be unit-tested at the boundary.
hazard.demonstration_of_effectiveness: TC-PUMP-115-A (boundary at 15 psi), TC-PUMP-115-B (alarm fires above limit).
hazard.residual_risk_acceptability: Acceptable; corrected inclusive comparison verified at the boundary reduces the probability of a missed occlusion to Remote.

requirements.text: The occlusion pressure-threshold comparison SHALL use an inclusive limit and SHALL be unit-tested at the boundary.

test_cases.expectedResults: Alarm fires at and above the inclusive limit.
Occlusion alarm fires.

design_docs.name: occlusion pressure-threshold evaluation - Software Design Description
design_docs.description:
The occlusion pressure-threshold evaluation module decides whether a measured line pressure constitutes an occlusion by comparing it against a configured limit. Its scope is the comparison semantics and the boundary handling of that decision; it does not sample the sensor or sound the alarm. As an IEC 62304 controlled component the comparison must be exact at its boundary, and under ISO 14971 it mitigates the hazard of a missed occlusion caused by an off-by-one or exclusive/inclusive error at the limit.

At runtime the module holds a below-limit state and an at-or-above-limit state, with the decision defined by an inclusive comparison at the configured limit. The design fails safe toward detection: at the exact limit the condition is treated as an occlusion, so a value sitting on the boundary is not silently discarded.

The decomposition comprises a threshold-configuration provider and a boundary comparator with defined inclusivity. Verification hooks include injectable pressures spanning the configured limit and an observable occlusion decision, so the test suite can assert the decision immediately below, at, and above the limit and confirm the boundary is handled inclusively.

user_needs.text: As a clinician, I need occlusion detection to be correct right at the threshold, so that a borderline blockage is not missed.

system_requirements.text: The infusion system SHALL evaluate the occlusion pressure threshold using an inclusive comparison verified at the boundary.

hazard.hazard: Spoofed telemetry masks an active alarm state.
hazard.hazardous_situation: A clinician relies on spoofed telemetry that hides an active alarm.
hazard.hazardous_sequence_of_events: 1. The pump publishes alarm/telemetry state to a remote monitor. 2. An attacker injects spoofed telemetry because message authenticity is not enforced. 3. The remote monitor shows a normal state. 4. The clinician's response to a real alarm is delayed.
hazard.software_related_causes: Telemetry message authenticity is not enforced (cybersecurity cause).
hazard.risk_control_measures: REQ-PUMP-116: telemetry messages SHALL be authenticated and integrity-protected.
hazard.demonstration_of_effectiveness: TC-PUMP-116-A (spoofed telemetry rejected), TC-PUMP-116-B (integrity failure raises a fault).
hazard.residual_risk_acceptability: Acceptable; authenticated telemetry reduces the probability of an accepted spoofed state to Remote. NOTE: the same missing message-authenticity control plausibly implies a distinct newly-identified hazardous situation - acceptance of spoofed control commands, not merely spoofed telemetry - which has not yet been captured as its own SHA row.

requirements.text: Telemetry messages SHALL be authenticated and integrity-protected before a remote monitor may display them.

test_cases.expectedResults: Message rejected; remote state unchanged.
Integrity fault raised.

design_docs.name: remote monitoring telemetry integrity - Software Design Description
design_docs.description:
The remote monitoring telemetry integrity module publishes alarm and status telemetry to a remote monitor and protects that telemetry from spoofing or tampering. Its scope is the authentication and integrity protection of outbound telemetry and the rejection of inauthentic inbound state; it does not itself alarm. As a network-exposed IEC 62304 controlled component its authenticity handling is security- and safety-relevant, and under ISO 14971 it mitigates the hazard of a clinician relying on a spoofed normal state that masks a real alarm.

At runtime the module holds a publishing state, a verifying state for any received or reflected state, and a rejecting state on an authentication or integrity failure. The design fails safe by refusing to present unverified telemetry as authoritative, so a spoofed or tampered message is discarded and flagged rather than displayed as truth.

The decomposition comprises a telemetry publisher, a message-authentication and integrity layer, and a verification-fault handler. Verification hooks include injectable spoofed and tampered messages and an observable accept/reject outcome, so the test suite can assert that unsigned telemetry is rejected and that a corrupted signed message raises an integrity fault.

user_needs.text: As a clinician relying on remote monitoring, I need the telemetry to be trustworthy, so that a spoofed normal reading cannot hide a real alarm from me.

system_requirements.text: The infusion system SHALL authenticate and integrity-protect monitoring telemetry before it is relied upon by a remote monitor.

hazard.hazard: Pump commits an unintended dose value.
hazard.hazardous_situation: The pump commits and delivers an unintended dose value.
hazard.hazardous_sequence_of_events: 1. Clinician types the dose. 2. Keypad debounce may drop a digit. 3. The committed dose is not independently cross-checked before delivery. 4. An unintended dose is delivered.
hazard.software_related_causes: (a) Keypad debounce may drop a keypress; (b) the committed dose is not independently cross-checked before delivery.
hazard.risk_control_measures: REQ-PUMP-117: keypad input SHALL apply a 20 ms debounce filter.
hazard.demonstration_of_effectiveness: TC-PUMP-117-A (debounce filtering), TC-PUMP-117-B (boundary: 20 ms chatter window).
hazard.residual_risk_acceptability: Acceptable; debounce filtering verified reduces dropped-digit probability to Remote.

requirements.text: Keypad input SHALL apply a 20 ms debounce filter to reject contact chatter.

test_cases.expectedResults: Only one keypress registered.

test_cases.setup: Fire presses at 19 ms and 21 ms.
test_cases.steps: 1. Press at 19 ms. 2. Press at 21 ms.
test_cases.expectedResults: 19 ms chatter rejected; 21 ms treated as a distinct press.

design_docs.name: keypad dose entry and debounce - Software Design Description
design_docs.description:
The keypad dose entry and debounce module captures clinician keystrokes for dose entry and rejects contact chatter. Its scope is reliable key capture and the debounce of physical contacts; it is one of several controls in the dose-entry path. As an IEC 62304 controlled component it must not silently drop or duplicate digits, and under ISO 14971 it mitigates one contributor to the hazard of an unintended committed dose value.

At runtime the module holds an idle state, a debouncing state during the configured settling window, and a keypress-accepted state; contacts that do not settle are discarded. It fails safe toward not fabricating input: chatter within the settling window yields a single keypress and never a phantom or dropped digit under nominal conditions. Note that independent confirmation of the fully committed dose is a separate control outside this module's scope.

The decomposition comprises a key-scan interface, a debounce filter with a configured window, and a keypress publisher. Verification hooks include injectable contact-chatter patterns and an observable keypress stream, so the test suite can assert that chatter within the window is collapsed to one press and that presses separated beyond the window are treated as distinct.

user_needs.text: As a clinician, I need the keypad to register exactly what I type, so that a dropped or duplicated digit does not commit an unintended dose.

system_requirements.text: The infusion system SHALL debounce keypad input so that contact chatter neither drops nor duplicates an entered digit.

hazard.hazard: Infusion context lost during a battery hot-swap.
hazard.hazardous_situation: Infusion context is lost during a battery hot-swap and delivery is interrupted or corrupted.
hazard.hazardous_sequence_of_events: 1. Mains power is removed and the battery is hot-swapped. 2. The power-fail handler must persist the infusion context to non-volatile memory. 3. On restore the context must be reloaded. 4. If not persisted, delivery state is corrupted.
hazard.software_related_causes: The power-fail handler may not persist the infusion context before the supercapacitor bridge expires.
hazard.harm: Interrupted or corrupted infusion; over- or under-dose.
hazard.risk_control_measures: Software mitigations are in place to preserve the infusion context across a battery hot-swap.
hazard.demonstration_of_effectiveness: TC-PUMP-118-A (context persisted on power-fail), TC-PUMP-118-B (boundary: bridge-time limit), TC-PUMP-118-C (negative: persistence failure alarms and stops).
hazard.residual_risk_acceptability: Acceptable; verified context persistence within the supercapacitor bridge time reduces corruption probability to Remote.

requirements.text: On power loss the pump SHALL persist the infusion context to non-volatile memory within the supercapacitor bridge time and SHALL reload it on power restore.

test_cases.expectedResults: Infusion context is reloaded intact.

test_cases.setup: Extend the outage to the bridge-time limit.
test_cases.expectedResults: Context persisted before the bridge expires.
Pump alarms and stops rather than resuming with corrupt state.

design_docs.name: power-fail infusion-context persistence - Software Design Description
design_docs.description:
The power-fail infusion-context persistence module preserves the active infusion context across a loss of primary power so that delivery can resume coherently. Its scope is the timely persistence of context to non-volatile storage on power loss and its reload on restore; it does not manage the battery itself. As an IEC 62304 controlled component the persistence must complete within the available hold-up time, and under ISO 14971 it mitigates the hazard of interrupted or corrupted delivery after a power interruption.

At runtime the module holds a running state, a persisting state triggered by a power-fail signal that writes context before the energy reserve is exhausted, and a reloading state on restore; a persistence failure drives an alarm-and-stop state. The design fails safe by alarming and stopping rather than resuming from an incomplete or corrupt context.

The decomposition comprises a power-fail detector, a context serializer, a non-volatile-store interface, and a reload/validation handler. Verification hooks include an injectable power-fail event, a controllable hold-up window, and injectable store faults, with an observable reloaded context and an observable alarm/stop outcome, so the test suite can assert context persistence within the hold-up window and an alarm-and-stop on a persistence fault.

user_needs.text: As a clinician, I need the pump to preserve its state across a brief power loss, so that a battery swap does not corrupt or silently interrupt the infusion.

system_requirements.text: The infusion system SHALL persist the active infusion context on power loss within the available hold-up time and reload it on power restore.
The infusion system SHALL alarm and stop rather than resume from an incomplete or corrupt infusion context.

hazard.hazard: Pump overheats without thermal shutdown.
hazard.hazardous_situation: The pump internal temperature exceeds the safe limit without a thermal shutdown.
hazard.hazardous_sequence_of_events: 1. Internal temperature rises. 2. The thermal-cutoff task must shut the pump down at 60 degrees C. 3. If it does not trigger, the pump continues to heat. 4. Drug degradation or a contact burn results.
hazard.software_related_causes: The thermal-cutoff task may not trigger shutdown at the 60 degrees C limit.
hazard.risk_control_measures: REQ-PUMP-119: the pump SHALL shut down and alarm when internal temperature exceeds 60 degrees C.
hazard.demonstration_of_effectiveness: TC-PUMP-119-A verifies the pump powers on and displays the current temperature.
hazard.residual_risk_acceptability: Acceptable; thermal cutoff bounds the maximum temperature, reducing the probability of overheating to Remote.

requirements.text: The pump SHALL shut down and alarm when internal temperature exceeds 60 degrees C.

test_cases.setup: Power on the pump at room temperature.
test_cases.expectedResults: The pump powers on and displays the current temperature.

design_docs.name: thermal cutoff and over-temperature shutdown - Software Design Description
design_docs.description:
The thermal cutoff and over-temperature shutdown module monitors internal temperature and shuts the device down when it exceeds a safe limit. Its scope is temperature evaluation and the commanded shutdown; it does not manage cooling. As an IEC 62304 controlled component the shutdown must be reliable at its limit, and under ISO 14971 it mitigates the hazard of drug degradation or a contact burn from an overheated device.

At runtime the module holds a monitoring state, a shutdown state entered when temperature exceeds the configured limit, and a sensor-fault state. It fails safe toward shutdown: an over-limit reading, and a sensor fault where temperature cannot be trusted, both drive the device to a safe non-operating condition with an alarm.

The decomposition comprises a temperature-sensor driver, a limit evaluator, a shutdown-command interface, and a sensor-health monitor. Verification hooks include an injectable temperature profile that crosses the configured limit and injectable sensor faults, with an observable shutdown and alarm state, so the test suite can drive temperature across the limit and assert that the shutdown hazard path actually triggers - not merely that the device powers on and displays a temperature.

user_needs.text: As a patient, I need the device to shut down if it overheats, so that I am not exposed to a burn or a degraded drug.

system_requirements.text: The infusion system SHALL shut down and alarm when internal temperature exceeds its configured safe limit.

hazard.hazard: Hard-limit override delivers an unsafe dose.
hazard.hazardous_situation: A hard-limit override allows an unsafe dose to be programmed and delivered.
hazard.hazardous_sequence_of_events: 1. Clinician attempts a dose above the hard limit. 2. The guardrail must block the override. 3. If the override is allowed without a second check, an unsafe dose is programmed. 4. Overdose results.
hazard.software_related_causes: The hard-limit override path may not require an independent second confirmation.
hazard.risk_control_measures: REQ-PUMP-120: a hard-limit override SHALL require an independent second-clinician confirmation and SHALL be logged.
hazard.demonstration_of_effectiveness: TC-PUMP-120-A (override blocked without second confirmation), TC-PUMP-120-B (boundary: at the hard limit), TC-PUMP-120-C (negative: override logged).
hazard.residual_risk_acceptability: Acceptable.

requirements.text: A hard-limit override SHALL require an independent second-clinician confirmation and SHALL be recorded in the audit log.

test_cases.expectedResults: Override blocked.

test_cases.setup: Program at and just above the hard limit.
test_cases.expectedResults: At limit allowed; above limit requires override with confirmation.
Override recorded in the audit log.

design_docs.name: dosing guardrails and hard-limit override - Software Design Description
design_docs.description:
The dosing guardrails and hard-limit override module enforces soft and hard dose limits and governs the controlled override of a hard limit. Its scope is limit enforcement and the override workflow with its audit trail; it does not compute the dose. As an IEC 62304 controlled component the override path must require independent authorization, and under ISO 14971 it mitigates the hazard of an unsafe dose delivered by bypassing a hard limit.

At runtime the module holds a within-limits state, a soft-limit-warning state, and a hard-limit-blocked state; an override is reachable only through an independent second-authorizer confirmation and is recorded. The design fails safe by blocking a hard-limit override that lacks the required independent confirmation, so a single actor cannot bypass a hard limit.

The decomposition comprises a limit evaluator, an override-authorization workflow, and an audit logger. Verification hooks include injectable dose values around the configured limits, a controllable second-authorizer signal, and a readable audit log, so the test suite can assert that a hard-limit override is blocked without independent confirmation, that behavior at the limit is correct, and that an authorized override is recorded.

user_needs.text: As a clinician, I need hard dose limits to require a second authorization to override, so that a single mistake cannot deliver an unsafe dose.

system_requirements.text: The infusion system SHALL require an independent second-authorizer confirmation to override a hard dose limit and SHALL record every override.
